papers.title: intmap: Fast and Flexible Mapping of Mobile DNA Integration for Basic and Translational Research
papers.summary: Abstract Summary Integration of exogenous DNA into host cell chromatin is a hallmark of many virus and transposon lifecycles and the foundational basis for many modern cellular and genetic therapies. Defining integration sites (ISs) in a population of cells can accordingly inform fundamental aspects of mobile DNA biology and therapeutic treatment outcomes. Here, we describe intmap, a software that generalizes IS analysis to diverse data-types and experimental systems. intmap functions independently of strict library design assumptions and is highly tunable with respect to analysis parameters. Using both simulated and experimental data, we show that IS mapping with intmap is fast, accurate, and highly flexible. Availability and implementation intmap, related documentation, and a convenient installation script are available at https://github.com/gbedwell/intmap . Additional information is provided in the online Supplement. Analysis commands, outputs, and other information related to this manuscript are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19475929

papers.title: MetaCCI: Meta Cell Cell Interaction inference and its application to CCIs characteristics of MDS
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Cell–cell interactions (CCIs) are fundamental to multicellular organisms and play crucial roles in diverse biological processes and disease mechanisms. Understanding CCIs is vital for deciphering disease pathogenesis and developing therapeutic strategies. Although numerous computational methods have been developed to infer CCIs from complex biological data, most existing approaches rely primarily on single-gene expression levels and ligand-receptor databases, often failing to capture the nuanced network-wide changes characteristic of disease states. Result We propose MetaCCI, a novel computational strategy that integrates meta-information into CCI inference by extending the traditional gene expression-based analysis to a gene regulatory network framework. MetaCCI meticulously combines established ligand-receptor pairs with quantitative insights into gene behavior within complex gene networks, enabling the precise extraction of relevant targets for CCI inference. Subsequently, CCI inference was performed using an eigen cell co-expression network, providing a more holistic view of cell-cell communication. Monte Carlo simulations demonstrated that MetaCCI consistently outperforms existing methods in CCI inference. We applied MetaCCI to characterize cell-cell communication in Myelodysplastic Syndromes (MDS). Our results identified distinct interaction patterns in MDS compared with normal cell populations, specifically highlighting the loss of CCIs between “Dendritic cells and Hematopoietic precursor cells” and between “Dendritic cells and Hematopoietic multipotent progenitor cells” as characteristic features of MDS. Furthermore, FABP5, CD63, and HMGB1 were identified as MDS-specific markers. These findings suggest that diminished CCIs involving dendritic cells, hematopoietic precursor cells, and multipotent progenitor cells are pivotal to MDS pathogenesis. Availability and implementation The MetaCCI software is freely available at https://github.com/HeewonGitHub/MetaCCI . An archived version of the software and example datasets used in this study is available at Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20101527

llm_highlights_zh: 理解细胞死亡机制对于揭示疾病的发生机理及制定治疗策略而言至关重要。
尽管已经开发出了许多计算方法，用于从复杂的生物数据中推断出细胞信号通路的变化，但现有的大多数方法主要依赖于单基因的表达水平以及配体-受体数据库，这些方法往往无法捕捉到疾病状态下所出现的、涉及整个网络层面的复杂变化。
我们提出了一种名为MetaCCI的新计算策略，该策略通过将传统的基于基因表达的分析方法扩展到基因调控网络框架中，从而将元信息融入到基因表达相关性分析的过程中。
papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
细胞间相互作用是多细胞生物体赖以生存的基础，其在多种生物学过程及疾病机制中发挥着至关重要的作用。深入理解这些相互作用对于揭示疾病的发生机制并制定治疗策略而言至关重要。尽管目前已开发出多种计算方法来从复杂的生物数据中推断细胞间相互作用，但现有方法大多仅依赖单基因表达水平及配体-受体数据库，往往无法捕捉到疾病状态下所出现的整体性网络变化。  

**研究方法与结果**  
我们提出了一种名为MetaCCI的新型计算策略，该策略通过将传统的基于基因表达的分析方法扩展到基因调控网络框架中，从而整合了元信息来辅助细胞间相互作用的推断。MetaCCI巧妙地结合了已知的配体-受体对与对复杂基因网络中基因行为的定量分析结果，使得相关靶标的精准识别成为可能。随后，我们利用特征化的细胞共表达网络进行了细胞间相互作用的进一步分析，这一方法为全面理解细胞间的通讯机制提供了有力支持。蒙特卡洛模拟结果表明，MetaCCI在细胞间相互作用推断方面的性能明显优于现有方法。我们将MetaCCI应用于骨髓增生异常综合征的研究中，发现该疾病状态下“树突状细胞与造血前体细胞”以及“树突状细胞与造血多能祖细胞”之间的相互作用模式发生了显著改变，这些变化被认为是骨髓增生异常综合征的重要特征。此外，FABP5、CD63和HMGB1等基因也被确认为与该疾病相关的特异性标志物。这些研究结果表明，涉及树突状细胞、造血前体细胞及多能祖细胞的细胞间相互作用减弱，是导致骨髓增生异常综合征发生的关键因素。  

**软件与数据资源**  
MetaCCI软件可免费获取，地址为：https://github.com/HeewonGitHub/MetaCCI。本研究使用的软件存档版本及示例数据集也可在Zenodo平台上找到，链接为：https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20101527。

all_papers.title: intmap: Fast and Flexible Mapping of Mobile DNA Integration for Basic and Translational Research
all_papers.summary: Abstract Summary Integration of exogenous DNA into host cell chromatin is a hallmark of many virus and transposon lifecycles and the foundational basis for many modern cellular and genetic therapies. Defining integration sites (ISs) in a population of cells can accordingly inform fundamental aspects of mobile DNA biology and therapeutic treatment outcomes. Here, we describe intmap, a software that generalizes IS analysis to diverse data-types and experimental systems. intmap functions independently of strict library design assumptions and is highly tunable with respect to analysis parameters. Using both simulated and experimental data, we show that IS mapping with intmap is fast, accurate, and highly flexible. Availability and implementation intmap, related documentation, and a convenient installation script are available at https://github.com/gbedwell/intmap . Additional information is provided in the online Supplement. Analysis commands, outputs, and other information related to this manuscript are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19475929

all_papers.title: MetaCCI: Meta Cell Cell Interaction inference and its application to CCIs characteristics of MDS
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Cell–cell interactions (CCIs) are fundamental to multicellular organisms and play crucial roles in diverse biological processes and disease mechanisms. Understanding CCIs is vital for deciphering disease pathogenesis and developing therapeutic strategies. Although numerous computational methods have been developed to infer CCIs from complex biological data, most existing approaches rely primarily on single-gene expression levels and ligand-receptor databases, often failing to capture the nuanced network-wide changes characteristic of disease states. Result We propose MetaCCI, a novel computational strategy that integrates meta-information into CCI inference by extending the traditional gene expression-based analysis to a gene regulatory network framework. MetaCCI meticulously combines established ligand-receptor pairs with quantitative insights into gene behavior within complex gene networks, enabling the precise extraction of relevant targets for CCI inference. Subsequently, CCI inference was performed using an eigen cell co-expression network, providing a more holistic view of cell-cell communication. Monte Carlo simulations demonstrated that MetaCCI consistently outperforms existing methods in CCI inference. We applied MetaCCI to characterize cell-cell communication in Myelodysplastic Syndromes (MDS). Our results identified distinct interaction patterns in MDS compared with normal cell populations, specifically highlighting the loss of CCIs between “Dendritic cells and Hematopoietic precursor cells” and between “Dendritic cells and Hematopoietic multipotent progenitor cells” as characteristic features of MDS. Furthermore, FABP5, CD63, and HMGB1 were identified as MDS-specific markers. These findings suggest that diminished CCIs involving dendritic cells, hematopoietic precursor cells, and multipotent progenitor cells are pivotal to MDS pathogenesis. Availability and implementation The MetaCCI software is freely available at https://github.com/HeewonGitHub/MetaCCI . An archived version of the software and example datasets used in this study is available at Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20101527

Understanding CCIs is vital for deciphering disease pathogenesis and developing therapeutic strategies. Although numerous computational methods have been developed to infer CCIs from complex biological data, most existing approaches rely primarily on single-gene expression levels and ligand-receptor databases, often failing to capture the nuanced network-wide changes characteristic of disease states. Result We propose MetaCCI, a novel computational strategy that integrates meta-information into CCI inference by extending the traditional gene expression-based analysis to a gene regulatory network framework. MetaCCI meticulously combines established ligand-receptor pairs with quantitative insights into gene behavior within complex gene networks, enabling the precise extraction of relevant targets for CCI inference. Subsequently, CCI inference was performed using an eigen cell co-expression network, providing a more holistic view of cell-cell communication. Monte Carlo simulations demonstrated that MetaCCI consistently outperforms existing methods in CCI inference. We applied MetaCCI to characterize cell-cell communication in Myelodysplastic Syndromes (MDS). Our results identified distinct interaction patterns in MDS compared with normal cell populations, specifically highlighting the loss of CCIs between “Dendritic cells and Hematopoietic precursor cells” and between “Dendritic cells and Hematopoietic multipotent progenitor cells” as characteristic features of MDS. Furthermore, FABP5, CD63, and HMGB1 were identified as MDS-specific markers. These findings suggest that diminished CCIs involving dendritic cells, hematopoietic precursor cells, and multipotent progenitor cells are pivotal to MDS pathogenesis.
all_papers.primary_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
细胞间相互作用是多细胞生物体赖以生存的基础，其在多种生物学过程及疾病机制中发挥着至关重要的作用。深入理解这些相互作用对于揭示疾病的发生机制并制定治疗策略而言至关重要。尽管目前已开发出多种计算方法来从复杂的生物数据中推断细胞间相互作用，但现有方法大多仅依赖单基因表达水平及配体-受体数据库，往往无法捕捉到疾病状态下所出现的整体性网络变化。  

**研究方法与结果**  
我们提出了一种名为MetaCCI的新型计算策略，该策略通过将传统的基于基因表达的分析方法扩展到基因调控网络框架中，从而整合了元信息来辅助细胞间相互作用的推断。MetaCCI巧妙地结合了已知的配体-受体对与对复杂基因网络中基因行为的定量分析结果，使得相关靶标的精准识别成为可能。随后，我们利用特征化的细胞共表达网络进行了细胞间相互作用的进一步分析，这一方法为全面理解细胞间的通讯机制提供了有力支持。蒙特卡洛模拟结果表明，MetaCCI在细胞间相互作用推断方面的性能明显优于现有方法。我们将MetaCCI应用于骨髓增生异常综合征的研究中，发现该疾病状态下“树突状细胞与造血前体细胞”以及“树突状细胞与造血多能祖细胞”之间的相互作用模式发生了显著改变，这些变化被认为是骨髓增生异常综合征的重要特征。此外，FABP5、CD63和HMGB1等基因也被确认为与该疾病相关的特异性标志物。这些研究结果表明，涉及树突状细胞、造血前体细胞及多能祖细胞的细胞间相互作用减弱，是导致骨髓增生异常综合征发生的关键因素。  

**软件与数据资源**  
MetaCCI软件可免费获取，地址为：https://github.com/HeewonGitHub/MetaCCI。本研究使用的软件存档版本及示例数据集也可在Zenodo平台上找到，链接为：https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20101527。
